limitations: March is a two-month stub; January is a full year. Neither combining them into 14 months nor multiplying March CFO by six yields TTM or normalized annual cash flow.

Revenue transition increases March professional-services revenue GBP204,716 and decreases deferred income equivalently. Prior comparatives are not restated. Exclusion is an analytical bridge, not a complete restatement to prior GAAP.

Section 20 changes EBIT and moves lease principal and interest cash to financing. Full old-basis EBIT needs rent/accrual details not disclosed; lease-adjusted CFO subtraction is a cash comparability bridge only.
Management strategic report says March operating profit GBP0.6m, but the audited P&L and arithmetic establish GBP60,223. Use statement figure.
OCR misreads March administration as GBP6,810,749 and cash FX as GBP184,446; visually verified amounts are GBP5,810,749 and GBP154,446.
Large debtor collection and creditor/deferred-income timing dominate CFO. Annual-billing seasonality is plausible, not established quantitatively by these two statements alone.
No direct reconciliation to US GAAP, post-close purchase accounting, Guidewire fiscal periods, consideration or acquisition-date cash is provided. Do not use historical cash as closing cash.
No target fair value, standalone DCF or durable post-synergy margin is supported by these accounts alone.
